correctness.rationale: For current rejection count \(r>0\), retaining every old rejected coordinate above \(c_r=K/(\alpha r)\) forces the next r-th order statistic above the e-BH rank-r threshold, so the next rejection count is at least r and every old coordinate remains above the no-larger new cutoff. Lowering one old coordinate below \(c_r\) while the other old coordinates equal \(c_r\) and outsiders are zero makes every rank fail. The affine continuation preserves the null supermartingale property by conditional expectation.

value.rationale: The result converts a qualitative freeze-after-rejection sufficient condition into a sharp quantitative continuation rule. It permits continued data collection on rejected hypotheses, gives the exact worst-case amount of evidence that must be protected, and shows the remainder is maximally exposable under the stated criterion. This directly addresses sample-allocation flexibility in sequential multiple testing rather than merely restating e-BH validity.
